name: Rice Brown Spot
description: A fungal disease causing brown spots on rice leaves, panicles, and grains. It is often associated with nutrient-deficient soils, especially low potassium and zinc. Brown spot was responsible for the Bengal famine of 1943 and remains an important disease in Africa.
symptoms: Small circular or oval brown spots on leaves
Spots with gray or whitish centers and reddish-brown margins
Lesions coalescing in severe infections causing leaf dieback
Dark brown spots on glumes and panicle branches
causes: Extended leaf wetness from rain or dew
Continuous rice cropping in poor soils
treatments: Apply fungicides containing mancozeb or propiconazole
Spray iprodione or carbendazim at heading stage
Apply potassium fertilizer to correct nutrient deficiency
Foliar spray of zinc sulfate (2g/L) for zinc-deficient fields
prevention: Maintain balanced soil fertility — adequate potassium and zinc
Use silicon-rich amendments (rice husk ash) to strengthen plants
Plant resistant or tolerant rice varieties
Use disease-free seeds treated with fungicide before planting
references: Africa Rice Brown Spot Management Guide
